metadata.title: The Watermark Is One Line of Code
metadata.subtitle: A git-explainer walkthrough of jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking — the KGW reference implementation
metadata.purpose: Walk the jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking GitHub repo with real git/wc data. Show that the marking mechanism is one line of code, that detection returns a p-value not a verdict, and that a commit labelled 'Documentation Updates' silently changed the detection statistic. Rung 1 throughout — all data from the local clone at books/lm-watermarking HEAD 8292251.
metadata.skill: git-explainer (descends from code-walkthrough; Claude bookends from ai-explainer)
metadata.source: jwkirchenbauer/lm-watermarking cloned 2026-08-12; HEAD 8292251 (2025-09-17). All data computed via git log, wc -l, git grep, git show. See REPO-VERIFY.md.
metadata.notes: Kokoro am_onyx, free (IN-FOR-BEAR LAW). GATE P before any ElevenLabs swap. Six GitHub skin scenes in fixed order: RepoHero, StructureMap, CallChain, Churn, CodeViewer, CodeDiff. Four Manim beats: B09 LOC hotspot, B23 vocab partition, B27 logit bars, B31 binomial null. Three CodeViewer slices: Slice A L62-80, Slice B L95-117, Slice C L153-164. Slice A range shortened from PLAN L54-80: L61 (assert, 135 chars) overflows the type floor; range starts at L62 to avoid elision. Slice B range shortened from L94-117: L94 (_bias_greenlist_logits def, 128 chars) overflows; range starts at L95. Lines L74, L78 (Slice A), L98, L113, L115 (Slice B) may clip at right edge at 26px mono — bytes in props are verbatim, display clipping is logged. KGW prohibition: no beat states or implies Anthropic's algorithm is this code. Never publish.

beats.narration_text: The word watermark comes from images, where there is a thing in the file you could point at. There is no such thing in the text. Nothing here is embedded.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — conceptual reframe: visible mark vs statistical bias

lines: Image watermark: a thing in the file you can point at.
Text watermark: a statistical property of token choices.
Nothing is embedded. No token is changed.
The mark is in the distribution, not in the data.

props.headline: Three functions. The key. The bias. The test.

beats.narration_text: Three functions. First: how the key and the previous token seed a fresh random partition of the vocabulary at every position.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — act map: key → partition → bias → detect

beats.narration_text: Animate how the green list is built at each token.
beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeComposerAsk ASK — vocab partition Manim before B23

props.command: Animate the KGW green list: 50,257-token vocabulary grid, γ=0.5 → 25,128 green tokens. Show the partition reshuffling at each of 6 successive token positions — same grid, new coloring each time.
props.segment: The Watermark Is One Line of Code

beats.narration_text: The green list is not stored anywhere. It's regenerated from scratch at every token, from the secret key times the previous token. Delete the key and it is unrecoverable.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — key insight: green list is ephemeral, not stored

lines: The green list is not stored anywhere.
Regenerated at every token: key × prev_token → RNG → partition.

beats.narration_text: Line 95: scores on the green list get plus greenlist_bias — which is delta, which is 2.0. That is the entire marking mechanism. Everything else in __call__ is batch handling, RNG setup, and the calls to the seeding and masking functions.
beats.new_visual_element: GitHubCodeViewer — Slice B, L95-117, watermark_processor.py, branch main

lines: def __call__(self, input_ids: torch.LongTensor, scores: torch.FloatTensor) -> torch.FloatTensor:
# this is lazy to allow us to colocate on the watermarked model's device
# NOTE, it would be nice to get rid of this batch loop, but currently,
# the seed and partition operations are not tensor/vectorized, thus
# each sequence in the batch needs to be treated separately.
props.caption: L95–117 · L95 is the watermark: +greenlist_bias on green scores (range shortened: L94 def overflows frame)

beats.narration_text: scores[greenlist_mask] = scores[greenlist_mask] + greenlist_bias. That is the watermark. One line. Add two to half the logits.
beats.new_visual_element: FormACard — dark card: the one line, isolated

lines: That is the watermark. One line.
Add two to half the logits.

beats.narration_text: Now the test. 200 tokens versus 40.
beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeComposerAsk ASK — binomial null before Manim B31

props.command: Plot the binomial null distribution for γ=0.5 at T=200 tokens. Mark the z_threshold=4.0 boundary. Show a realistic watermarked observed count and its z-score. Then repeat for T=40 tokens — show that the test has no statistical power to detect.
props.segment: The Watermark Is One Line of Code

beats.narration_text: Detection is scipy.stats.norm.sf(z). It returns a p-value. A p-value is not a verdict, and asking to see the watermark is like asking to see the loadedness of a single die roll.

props.headline: A commit that said 'Documentation Updates' and wasn't.

beats.narration_text: Buried in the WatermarkDetector __init__ signature: the default value of ignore_repeated_bigrams changed from False to True. That is not documentation.
